title: fix(microsoft-foundry): correct limits for new GPT-5 deployments
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes undersized context and output limits when Microsoft Foundry creates configuration for documented GPT-5 model families, including GPT-5 mini deployment aliases.

## User Impact

New configurations for the known GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.3 Codex families receive 400,000 context tokens and 128,000 output tokens. Existing configured limits survive model selection and runtime normalization, including deliberate 128,000/16,384 caps with canonical model identity already present. Previously generated undersized entries remain unchanged and can be adjusted explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact-family resolver in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts:206` only covered GPT-5.4 mini/nano in the 400K family. Older documented families fell through to the generic 128K/16K fallback. Extend that existing mapping while preserving the separate large-context families, chat models, and unknown-model fallback.

This rewrite omits the old PR's automatic persisted-limit repair: canonical model identity does not establish who chose the limits, and normal normalization adds that identity itself. It also defers the disputed Codex Max reasoning change. No migration, new setting, or reasoning-policy change is included.

## Evidence

- Against main `e3d396280fc8bb99646edd83b7aa09c48988b18b`, the final capacity matrix produced **12 intended failures / 14 passes** (352.14 seconds Vitest; 628.03 seconds wall including worker preparation and verification). With the fix, both final test files passed: **67/67 tests**.
- Focused command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Fixed run: 236.86 seconds Vitest, 309.65 seconds wall. Worker preparation and imports dominate this run; the cases exercise the production configuration builder and existing provider hooks without a live service.
- Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Delta from main: production **+5/-1 (net +4)**; tests **+68/-22 (net +46)**. The capacity matrix moved to the shared-builder test file to keep the provider suite within its line budget. No runtime repair helper is added.
- Exact-head PR CI passed for `9390eec842d94a2962d130eaf940ba8cf9e05144`: [run 40068250988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40068250988). Older superseded runs remain red in the raw GitHub rollup.
- Prior [read-only discovery/configuration evidence](https://github.com/snotty/openclaw/blob/9bc29d4338ff9573b621feb2047b806c49783be7/.github/proofs/foundry-continuation-config-proof.json) identifies GPT-5 mini. Live Azure discovery and inference were not rerun for this head; the new proof uses synthetic deployment metadata through the production configuration builder.

ClawSweeper reviewed the current head with no code findings. No stable-upgrade run was performed: this patch changes new-entry defaults and does not alter schemas, loaders, or persisted-limit normalization; the production-hook tests above verify preservation of existing caps. Its additional upgrade-proof request remains an explicit gap for the maintainer’s land decision.
